title: Tip, Tap and Toe's Sentry Dance
summary: Green recalls the three dancers dressed in soldiers' leggings and crowns as the Rhythm Kings, who were clever tap dancers.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So let's go on to other people that were in the Hoofer's Club. I had mentioned before Tip, Tap and Toe. What did they bring to the Hoofer's Club?

Well, they brought what they called the Sentry Dance. You remember in the United States Armed Forces they used to wear these cloth leggings, where they wrapped this piece of cloth around the leg, all the way up, like a sock? Well, they was dressed as soldiers, you know, the three of them, you see. And they called themselves -- they was dressed in soldiers suits and they would wear a crown on their head, you see, as a hat. It was like some kind of crown. So that's why they called themselves the Rhythm Kings.
Were they comedy as well? You say
No, no. They was just clever tap dancers.
